text: A strain of Bacillus sp (Bacillus R-4) produces a protease and a carbohydrolase both of which have the ability to lyse Rhizopus cell walls. Of the enzymes, the carbohydrolase has been purified to an ultracentrifugally and electrophoretically homogeneous state, and identified as a chitosanase. The enzyme was active on glycol chitosan as well as chitosan. Molecular weight of the purified enzyme was estimated as 31, 000 and isoelectric point as pH 8.30. The enzyme was most active at pH 5.6 and at 40 degrees Celsius with either Rhizopus cell wall or glycol chitosan as substrate, and was stable over a range of pH 4.5 to 7.5 at 40 degrees Celsius for 3 hours. The activity was lost by sulfhydryl reagents and restored by either reduced glutathione or L-cysteine. An abrupt decrease in viscosity of the reaction mixture suggested an endogenous cleavage of chitosan by this enzyme.
